title: Forgel Code: interactive agent client instead of a command wrapper
request: The Forgel Code client stops being only a set of one-shot, argument-driven wrappers. Opened without arguments it starts an interactive session in which the owner describes work in plain language, reads the agent's answers, follows the plan and the progress of tasks and releases, and accepts work or sends it back with remarks without leaving the session. Adopting a repository, creating a project, secrets and configuration stay explicit. One-shot scripted usage and its machine-readable output remain unchanged, and the client stays thin: the model, the sandbox, independent checks, review and releases stay in the engine. The requirements below follow the existing feature document named by the owner and the client's documented contract; they are behaviour, not implementation.

audit.summary: The release is not publishable: the interactive session's redactor leaks secrets in common engine output forms, including quoted labels, newline-separated values, and values beginning with punctuation. The client also retains raw engine text in session memory, changes the existing --help output, and polls the engine at a rate that does not satisfy the quiet/cheap idle requirement. The existing test suites pass but do not exercise these cases.

findings.issue: Quoted secret labels are not fully redacted. For a message such as `'token': 'abc123'` (and the equivalent JSON double-quoted form), `_binding` treats the closing quote of the label as the opening quote of the value, so `_span` masks only the separator and leaves `abc123` visible. This violates the requirement that the secret value be absent from displayed text.
findings.suggestion: Handle a closing quote after a quoted label before looking for the separator, or parse quoted keys and values; add tests for quoted labels and JSON snippets and assert the value is absent from captured output.

findings.issue: Redaction misses values separated from a secret label by a newline and values beginning with punctuation that `_NOT_A_VALUE` rejects. `_SPACES` covers only space and tab, so a label followed by a newline and a value is not masked; after an explicit colon or equals, `token: !abc123` and `token: [abc123]` are also shown unchanged. This violates the colon/whitespace masking criterion and can display the credential.
findings.suggestion: Treat all whitespace including line breaks as separators between label, separator and value, and do not reject the first value character after an explicit colon or equals. Add direct and session-level tests for newline-separated and punctuation-prefixed values.

findings.issue: The session keeps unredacted engine text in memory. `show_state` assigns the raw joined state to `self.last_state`, and `idle_refresh` assigns raw `exc.message` to `self.idle_failure`; if engine output or an error contains key material, it remains in the client for the session, violating the requirement that secrets never appear in anything the client keeps.
findings.suggestion: Store the redacted form, or a hash, for comparison and deduplication, and never assign raw engine text to long-lived session attributes.

findings.issue: The parser description was changed, so `forgel-code --help` no longer produces its previous output. Requirement 13 and acceptance 12 require every existing non-interactive usage to keep its previous behavior, output and exit status.
findings.suggestion: Revert the parser description to the previous text and document the new no-argument behavior only in README/CHANGELOG, or update the compatibility requirement explicitly.

findings.issue: Idle refresh is not cheap. `IDLE_REFRESH_SECONDS` is 0.5 and each `idle_refresh` calls `read_state`, which runs the engine's `tasks` and `status` commands; an idle session therefore performs about four engine calls per second while the owner waits, contrary to the requirement that machine work stay essentially unchanged during idle waiting.
findings.suggestion: Use a much longer poll interval or backoff, or an engine-side blocking/event mechanism, and verify the idle-work requirement.

findings.issue: An idle state update is written directly after the already-printed prompt, so the state's first line appears on the prompt line and can interleave with text already typed. The review itself notes this. It does not match the normal state display and can disturb the visible input line.
findings.suggestion: Print a newline or redraw the prompt around idle updates, and keep the owner's partially typed line intact.
